messages.subject: How to feed different temps into environ
parts:
Dear all

I’m a little confused as to how some of the data from micro metout feeds into the ecto environ dataframe.

I’ve changed TALOC TAREF and TSKY to be in line with recorded values (pretty warm – Tennessee), but until the sun has risen, the environ table shows TCs around 0 Celsius, and TSUB jumps from 0 for 6 hours to 19 high numbers as the sun begins to rise.

I considered setting SOLR and ZEN to full, but that greatly limits how I can use the package.

Any advice?

Cheers,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: How to feed different temps into environ
parts:
Hi Alex,

It's hard to know what's wrong without some example code. The ectotherm model expects input tables called metout, soil, shadmet and shadsoil which by default are passed in as e.g.:
 metout = micro$metout

So you can either alter micro$metout before calling the ectotherm model or make your own metout table and pass that in directly. You may already know this, but the environ table is what the organism is exposed to and will vary depending whether th organism is above or below ground.

Here is an example of how to override e.g. TALOC to be a constant 40 deg C:

library(NicheMapR)

micro <- micro_global()

ecto <- ectotherm()
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$TC, type = 'l')

micro$metout[, 3] <- 40 # change TALOC, column 3, to 40 deg

ecto <- ectotherm()
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$TC, type = 'l')

All the best,
Mike

parts:
Hi Alex,

You were changing the values correctly but the main issue is how you set up the microclimate model. You specified the reference height the same as the local height - you shouldn't change the reference height as it is referring to the height the macroclimate data (air temp, wind speed, humidity) were recorded at. I really shouldn't have made it an option to change in the micro_ functions. Also, the depths must be roughly similar to the defaults, going to about 2m maximum and spaced logarithmically, i.e. the spacing increasing with depth. Finally, you selected 'runshade = 0' which you shouldn't do if you're running the ectotherm model, which expects two shade scenarios as input, i.e. from metout and shadmet, soil and shadsoil, etc.

I think you'll find once you've fixed those issues with the microclimate model, it should all make sense. E.g. run it like:
micro <- micro_global(loc = longlat, timeinterval = timeinterval, soiltype = 5, elev = 961, runmoist = 0, nyears = nyears, runshade = 1, minshade = 0, clearsky = 1, run.gads = 1, IR = 0, soilgrids = 0, Usrhyt = 0.005, slope = 0, aspect = 0, REFL = 0.15)

Note some of the ectotherm model parameter settings you've specified are not needed if you're not running the DEB model. I.e. CTKILL onwards in your list.

All the best,
Mike

You were changing the values correctly but the main issue is how you set up the microclimate model. You specified the reference height the same as the local height - you shouldn't change the reference height as it is referring to the height the macroclimate data (air temp, wind speed, humidity) were recorded at. I really shouldn't have made it an option to change in the micro_ functions. Also, the depths must be roughly similar to the defaults, going to about 2m maximum and spaced logarithmically, i.e. the spacing increasing with depth. Finally, you selected 'runshade = 0' which you shouldn't do if you're running the ectotherm model, which expects two shade scenarios as input, i.e. from metout and shadmet, soil and shadsoil, etc.

I think you'll find once you've fixed those issues with the microclimate model, it should all make sense. E.g. run it like:
micro <- micro_global(loc = longlat, timeinterval = timeinterval, soiltype = 5, elev = 961, runmoist = 0, nyears = nyears, runshade = 1, minshade = 0, clearsky = 1, run.gads = 1, IR = 0, soilgrids = 0, Usrhyt = 0.005, slope = 0, aspect = 0, REFL = 0.15)

Note some of the ectotherm model parameter settings you've specified are not needed if you're not running the DEB model. I.e. CTKILL onwards in your list.

It's hard to know what's wrong without some example code. The ectotherm model expects input tables called metout, soil, shadmet and shadsoil which by default are passed in as e.g.:
 metout = micro$metout

So you can either alter micro$metout before calling the ectotherm model or make your own metout table and pass that in directly. You may already know this, but the environ table is what the organism is exposed to and will vary depending whether th organism is above or below ground.

Here is an example of how to override e.g. TALOC to be a constant 40 deg C:

library(NicheMapR)

micro <- micro_global()

ecto <- ectotherm()
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$TC, type = 'l')

micro$metout[, 3] <- 40 # change TALOC, column 3, to 40 deg

ecto <- ectotherm()
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$TC, type = 'l')

Hi Alex,

You were changing the values correctly but the main issue is how you set up the microclimate model. You specified the reference height the same as the local height - you shouldn't change the reference height as it is referring to the height the macroclimate data (air temp, wind speed, humidity) were recorded at. I really shouldn't have made it an option to change in the micro_ functions. Also, the depths must be roughly similar to the defaults, going to about 2m maximum and spaced logarithmically, i.e. the spacing increasing with depth. Finally, you selected 'runshade = 0' which you shouldn't do if you're running the ectotherm model, which expects two shade scenarios as input, i.e. from metout and shadmet, soil and shadsoil, etc.

I think you'll find once you've fixed those issues with the microclimate model, it should all make sense. E.g. run it like:
micro <- micro_global(loc = longlat, timeinterval = timeinterval, soiltype = 5, elev = 961, runmoist = 0, nyears = nyears, runshade = 1, minshade = 0, clearsky = 1, run.gads = 1, IR = 0, soilgrids = 0, Usrhyt = 0.005, slope = 0, aspect = 0, REFL = 0.15)

Note some of the ectotherm model parameter settings you've specified are not needed if you're not running the DEB model. I.e. CTKILL onwards in your list.

All the best,
Mike

Hi Alex,

It's hard to know what's wrong without some example code. The ectotherm model expects input tables called metout, soil, shadmet and shadsoil which by default are passed in as e.g.:
 metout = micro$metout

So you can either alter micro$metout before calling the ectotherm model or make your own metout table and pass that in directly. You may already know this, but the environ table is what the organism is exposed to and will vary depending whether th organism is above or below ground.

Here is an example of how to override e.g. TALOC to be a constant 40 deg C:

library(NicheMapR)

micro <- micro_global()

ecto <- ectotherm()
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$TC, type = 'l')

micro$metout[, 3] <- 40 # change TALOC, column 3, to 40 deg

ecto <- ectotherm()
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$TC, type = 'l')

All the best,
Mike

Hi Alex,

OK thanks for the context. If burrowing is an option, they'll go there when they're not in their active phase, or if temperature are too extreme at the surface. If you allow activity all the time, i.e. nocturnal, diurnal and crepuscular, you'll only see them go underground if conditions are extreme on the surface. Also note that by keeping relative humidity constant and varying temperature, you're actually varying the absolute humidity which I'm guessing is not what you want. Finally, the reason relative humidity was changing was actually because you hadn't changed the shadmet TALOC column and, for the reason just mentioned, the relative humidity was changing. I.e. the model is adjusting humidity for the new air temps in the shade on the assumption that the absolute humidity isn't changing. So there was nothing odd going on in the model (phew!). You just missed putting shadmet rather than metout in your code.

All the best,
Mike

You were changing the values correctly but the main issue is how you set up the microclimate model. You specified the reference height the same as the local height - you shouldn't change the reference height as it is referring to the height the macroclimate data (air temp, wind speed, humidity) were recorded at. micro <- micro_global(loc = longlat, timeinterval = timeinterval, soiltype = 5, elev = 961, runmoist = 0, nyears = nyears, runshade = 1, minshade = 0, clearsky = 1, run.gads = 1, IR = 0, soilgrids = 0, Usrhyt = 0.005, slope = 0, aspect = 0, REFL = 0.15)

Hi Alex,

It's hard to know what's wrong without some example code. The ectotherm model expects input tables called metout, soil, shadmet and shadsoil which by default are passed in as e.g.:
 metout = micro$metout

So you can either alter micro$metout before calling the ectotherm model or make your own metout table and pass that in directly. You may already know this, but the environ table is what the organism is exposed to and will vary depending whether th organism is above or below ground.

Here is an example of how to override e.g. TALOC to be a constant 40 deg C:

library(NicheMapR)

micro <- micro_global()

ecto <- ectotherm()
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$TC, type = 'l')

micro$metout[, 3] <- 40 # change TALOC, column 3, to 40 deg

ecto <- ectotherm()
environ <- as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
plot(environ$TC, type = 'l')
